title: Will vs. No Will Simulation
learning_objectives: Visualize specific consequences of dying with versus without a will
Calculate financial impact of probate and intestacy
Understand timeline differences between planned and unplanned estates
Recognize how unintended inheritances harm families
description: Interactive simulator showing side-by-side outcomes for three scenarios: with a will versus dying intestate. Students track asset distribution, costs, timeline, and family impact.
instructions: Analyze three scenarios showing outcomes with and without a will
Compare asset distribution between will-directed and intestate succession
Calculate total costs including probate, legal fees, and delays
Identify family impacts and unintended consequences
Reflect on when a will becomes non-negotiable

scenarios.name: Single Person, Age 26
scenarios.description: Young professional with serious partner, no will

details.relationship_status: Serious partner (Emma), dating 3 years, planning to marry

with_will.asset_distribution: All assets to Emma per will
with_will.family_impact: Emma receives assets smoothly, wishes honored, minimal conflict

without_will.asset_distribution: All assets to parents per {{STATE_NAME}} intestacy law (Emma receives $0)
without_will.family_impact: Emma evicted from shared apartment, loses all possessions, engagement ring claimed by parents, partner of 3 years gets nothing

scenarios.name: Married Couple with Children
scenarios.description: Young parents, two children, no guardian designation

with_will_guardians.guardianship: Children immediately to designated guardians (Lisa's brother and wife)
with_will_guardians.asset_management: Life insurance to testamentary trust for children's benefit
with_will_guardians.timeline: Guardians take custody within days; trust established within 3 months
with_will_guardians.family_impact: Children stay with familiar extended family, financial security through trust, minimal disruption during trauma

without_will_guardians.guardianship: Children temporarily in foster care while court decides custody
without_will_guardians.custody_battle: Maternal grandmother vs. paternal aunt petition for custody
without_will_guardians.timeline: 6 months of legal battle, children in limbo
without_will_guardians.family_impact: Children traumatized by temporary foster care and uncertainty, family relationships damaged by custody battle, life insurance in lump sum to grandmother (winner) with no trust management

details.relationship_status: Divorced 2 years ago, remarried 1 year ago
details.will_status: Created 10 years ago, still names ex-spouse Jennifer as beneficiary; never updated

updated_will.asset_distribution: Assets to trust for child's benefit
updated_will.family_impact: Child financially secure, raised by designated guardian, current wife (Angela) receives personal items

outdated_will.asset_distribution: All assets to ex-wife Jennifer per old will
outdated_will.guardian_situation: Brad's brother has custody but zero financial resources
outdated_will.legal_battle: Current wife Angela sues to challenge will; 18-month battle
outdated_will.family_impact: Ex-wife gets $275K despite remarriage; current wife gets nothing; child's guardian (Brad's brother) has no resources; family relationships destroyed; child caught in middle of legal battle

analysis_questions.question: Which scenario's intestacy outcome surprised you most? Why?
Calculate the cost difference between having and not having proper estate planning for Scenario B:
What's the hidden cost beyond money in these scenarios?
analysis_questions.sample_answer: Family trauma, damaged relationships, children's psychological harm, uncertainty during grief, unintended consequences

analysis_questions.question: At what life stage does a will become absolutely non-negotiable?
analysis_questions.sample_answer: When you have children (guardian designation), serious relationship, or significant assets

analysis_questions.question: What life events require immediate will updates?

key_takeaways: Dying without a will means the state decides who gets your assets and raises your children
Unmarried partners have NO inheritance rights without a will—even after decades together
Outdated wills can be worse than no will—always update after major life changes
Guardian designation is the most critical part of a will for parents
The cost of creating a will ($300-800) is trivial compared to the cost of intestacy
In {{STATE_NAME}}, intestacy laws follow {{STATE_NAME}} probate code formulas

assessment.formative: Scenario analysis completion and cost calculations
assessment.reflection: Personal determination of when will becomes essential for their life stage
